text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Ankara hints it may boycott German companies in Turkey in retaliation for Germany's opposition to Turkish membership of European Union.
- Iranian Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati says Iran is determined to put an end to the tension between the two countries on his visit to Ankara.
- Turkish secularists and Islamists treat Velayati differently.
- Duff and Phelps international credit rating agencies downgrades Turkish banks' credit note.
- Coalition partner Tansu Ciller is trying to keep her conservative True Path Party together in face of opposition to Islamist wing of government.
- Parliament will debate a security report on Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) camps in Iranian territory.
- Turkey's state-run pipeline company Botas sees an oil pipeline between Egypt and southern Turkey as feasible.
- Iraqi Kurdish peace committee meets in Ankara on Tuesday.
